# External dataset calibration report

Generated by `external/calibrate_from_external.py`. Values below come from real public data; everything not listed here (steps, SpO2, temperature, stressed/anomaly labels) is still synthetic.

## Accelerometer activity_index (x^2 + y^2 + z^2 of one sample, in g)

| Species | State | n samples | mean | sd | p5 | median | p95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cat | resting | 1,331,811 | 1.004 | 0.058 | 0.971 | 1.004 | 1.034 |
| cat | active | 445,588 | 1.329 | 1.137 | 0.33 | 1.028 | 3.214 |
| dog | resting | 198,868 | 1.033 | 0.131 | 0.909 | 1.026 | 1.172 |
| dog | active | 145,489 | 1.536 | 1.636 | 0.098 | 1.053 | 4.648 |

- **cat:** only 49.3% of active samples exceed the resting 95th percentile, so one accelerometer sample separates rest from activity poorly. Steps or a windowed measure must carry most of that distinction.
- **dog:** only 42.7% of active samples exceed the resting 95th percentile, so one accelerometer sample separates rest from activity poorly. Steps or a windowed measure must carry most of that distinction.

## Dog resting heart rate (Invoxia, per-dog median of heart-rate segments)

40 dogs, 15,779 segments; 5th/50th/95th percentile: [44.0, 60.1, 80.9] (assumed bpm - confirm against the dataset README).

| Size class | dogs | median HR | IQR | literature baseline | gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | 6 | 59.7 | 56.5-69.7 | 110 | -50.3 |
| medium | 28 | 59.7 | 55.6-67.5 | 90 | -30.3 |
| large | 6 | 52.4 | 47.0-62.1 | 75 | -22.6 |

Linear fit: HR = 74.58 + -0.44 x weight(kg) + -1.246 x age(yr), residual sd 8.8 bpm; correlation with weight -0.29, with age -0.18.
